articles.title: A $2 MILLION EXPLOIT LEADS TO A $3.7 MILLION FREE-FOR-ALL
articles.summary: An attacker used a privileged bridge-minter role to mint billions, then quintillions, of unbacked ACE on BNB Chain and sold them for about $2M, crashing the price to around $0.0001 against roughly $0.04 on exchanges. Traders then bought the cheap tokens and sent them through Fusionist's bridge, emptying its 53.7 million real ACE (about $3.7M) across 24 addresses. One wallet turned about $50 into $17,670. About $1.87M of the attacker's proceeds went through Tornado Cash. Fusionist told followers to pause ACE activity on BSC and hasn't updated since, and Gate rolled back ACE/USDT trades, leaving some users with negative balances, and will delist its ACE perp. ACE is down about 20%.

articles.title: KALSHI FACES MONDAY HEARING ON NEW YORK ORDER
articles.summary: A federal judge denied the CFTC's second emergency bid to block New York AG Letitia James' enforcement case, clearing the way for a state judge to hear her request for a temporary restraining order on Monday at 11:30 AM ET. The proposed order would bar Kalshi from operating "within or from New York," which Kalshi says would shut down its exchange for every customer and force liquidation of open positions, while James' office says that isn't its goal. Federal appeals courts are split, with the Fourth, Sixth, and Ninth Circuits siding with states and the Third with Kalshi, so the fight could reach the Supreme Court. The CFTC and DOJ have a separate suit against New York pending since April.

articles.title: BACKPACK COMPLETES CFTC TRIPLE LICENSE STACK: DCO, DCM, AND FCM
articles.summary: Backpack secured NFA approval for a Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) license, completing the full CFTC regulatory trifecta alongside its Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) and Designated Contract Market (DCM) designations approved earlier this week. With all three licenses held in-house, Backpack can operate as broker, exchange, and clearinghouse without routing through third-party intermediaries, a vertical stack Kraken assembled via $550M in acquisition costs. Only two other US firms, Kraken and Kalshi, hold equivalent in-house clearing capacity for leveraged perpetuals. The Solana-based exchange positions itself as the first CFTC-regulated venue to offer leveraged perps with unified global liquidity onshore, with a waitlist now open for early access.

articles.title: TEMPO LAUNCHES ALTERNATIVE X402 FACILITATOR
articles.summary: Tempo released an alternative facilitator for the x402 machine payment protocol, allowing developers to accept USDC or Base payments while routing settlements through Tempo's network rather than Coinbase's official facilitator. Migration from the reference implementation requires a single URL change, lowering switching costs for existing x402 service operators. The launch, endorsed by Paradigm's Georgios Konstantopoulos, introduces direct competition for x402's settlement layer and reduces developer dependence on Coinbase's infrastructure for agentic payment routing.

articles.title: ANATOMY OF A FILL: PROPAMMS ON ETHEREUM
articles.summary: PropAMMs, live on Ethereum mainnet since May, decouple the 12-second Ethereum slot clock from the quote clock by letting a single market maker stream signed price updates to block builders, cutting stale-price exposure from up to 12 seconds to roughly 1 second per fill. Fermi and Metric together cleared $458M in the week of September 14-20, capturing 7.6% of Uniswap's $6B that week, with Fermi turning over its $5.4M liquidity pool 23 times daily versus Uniswap v3's 0.6x. The design shifts ordering authority to four builders (Titan, Quasar, BuilderNet, and Bombora) operating on voluntary commitments with no protocol enforcement, Titan alone routing 69% of propAMM trades while producing 44% of blocks. ERC-8324 proposes standardization but remains undeployed, while PropAMMs account for roughly 40% of volume on the largest Solana venues and 5-10% on Ethereum mainnet.

articles.title: HOW DO PEOPLE EARN FROM THE AI ECONOMY?
articles.summary: Agents can expand what individuals can do and let more people share in the AI economy. They can handle discovery, coordination, and payment. Visa says its nearly 5 billion payment credentials can verify that an agent is authorized by an accountable person through its Trusted Agent Protocol, now extending to agent wallets and task marketplaces including Taskmarket. It launched Visa CLI to US users as an experimental agent wallet for OUSD, built on Tempo and the Machine Payments Protocol. Visa has invited wallet and marketplace builders to integrate.

articles.title: EIGEN FALLS 48% IN FOUR WEEKS, LAGGING BITCOIN, ETHER
articles.summary: EIGEN fell 48% over four weeks, lagging both Bitcoin and Ether, as EigenLayer's restaking collateral contracted 28.5% to $4.52 billion from its October 21 level. Token unlock pressure, with large tranches of EIGEN becoming liquid, combined with reduced appetite for restaking yield in the current rate environment, drove the sell-off. EigenLayer's EigenCloud product launched during the drawdown but did not stem the decline.

articles.title: THE AGENTIC STORY ON THE EVE OF THE 2026 HOLIDAY SEASON
articles.summary: Stripe reports daily spend on Link Agent Wallet, which powers Muse, Instinct and Grok, was nearly 80 times higher in mid-November than at the start of September, and doubled in the last month. Over 40% of volume last week was airfare, travel, and lodging, about a third retail, and a quarter other categories. More than half of consumers who make one agentic purchase make a second, typically in the same category. Stripe plans more updates around Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

articles.title: SOME SIMPLE ECONOMICS OF AGI: VERIFICATION IS THE BOTTLENECK
articles.summary: MIT economist and Libra/Diem co-creator Christian Catalini releases a distilled paper arguing verification, not compute, is the binding constraint on safe AI scaling, a thesis nine months of evidence has validated.
